verses.1: And after that, Jesus traveled through Galilee. He didn’t want to travel through Judea, because the Jews wanted to kill him there.
verses.2: But the Passover of the Jews was a time of celebration and joy.
verses.3: So his brothers said to him, “Turn around and go to Judea. Then your disciples will see for themselves what you do.”
verses.4: After all, no one can truly do anything in secret, nor can they expect to be recognized for their actions. If you do such things, then show yourself to the world.
verses.5: Nor did his brothers believe in him at all.
verses.6: So Jesus says to them: “My time is not yet come. But your time has already been prepared.”
verses.7: The world cannot hate you; only I do. I hate you because I testify about him that his deeds are evil.
verses.8: You have gone to the feast. I will not go to this feast, because my time has not yet come.
verses.9: After saying these things, he remained in Galilee.
verses.10: And when his brothers went up to the feast, he also went up, not openly, but in a secret manner.
verses.11: So, the Jews waited for him during the meal and said, “Where is he?”
verses.12: And there was much disagreement among the people about him. Some said that he was good, while others said, “Yes, but he’s misleading the crowd.”
verses.13: But no one dared speak about him out of fear of the Jews.
verses.14: And as the feast was in progress, Jesus went into the temple and began to teach.
verses.15: So, the Jews marveled, saying, “How could he know these letters without learning them?”
verses.16: Then Jesus said to them, “It is not I who teach, but the one who sent me.
verses.17: If anyone wants to fulfill his own desires, then it will be clear whether those desires come from God or from himself.
verses.18: He who speaks without self-interest seeks his own glory. But the one who seeks the glory of the one who sent him is truly righteous; there is no injustice in him at all.
verses.19: Did not Moses give you this law? And no one among you can carry out this law by himself. Why do you want me to be killed?
verses.20: The crowd said, “You have demons in you. Who wants to kill you?”
verses.21: Jesus replied to them, “I have done a work, and all of you will be amazed.”
verses.22: Therefore, Moses gave you the command to be circumcised. It isn’t that it comes from Moses himself, but rather from our ancestors. On the Sabbath day, you should circumcise a person.
verses.23: If a person takes an oath on the Sabbath in order not to break Moses’ law, then why do you think I have created a healthy person in the Sabbath?
verses.24: Do not judge by appearance, but judge fairly.
verses.25: So, some people from the Jerusalemites said: “Isn’t this the person they want to get rid of?”
verses.26: And see how they speak nonsense, and tell him nothing true. Perhaps the rulers really knew that this person was indeed the Christ.
verses.27: But we know where he comes from. When Christ comes, no one will know where he comes from.
verses.28: So, in the temple, Jesus began to teach and said, “Do you know where I come from? I have not left my own home. It is truly true that He who sent me has sent me; but you do not know Him.”
verses.29: I know that he sent me away along with him.
verses.30: They tried to catch him, but no one touched him at all. Otherwise, his hour would have arrived.
verses.31: Many from the crowd believed in him. They said, “When Christ comes, will he do more signs than these?”
verses.32: The Pharisees heard that the crowd was gathered around him, so they sent the high priests and the Pharisee’s officials to arrest him.
verses.33: So said Jesus: “I will still be with you for a little while longer. I will go before those who sent me.”
verses.34: You will seek me, but you will not find me. And where I am, you yourselves cannot go.
verses.35: So, the Jews said to themselves, “Where will he go? Won’t he find that we haven’t yet found him? Won’t he go out into the midst of the Greeks and teach them?”
verses.36: What is the meaning of this statement? “Ask me, and you won’t find any answer. And where can I go, if you yourselves cannot come to me?”
verses.37: On the last day of the great feast, Jesus appeared. He said, “If anyone wants to come to me, let him come and drink from my cup.”
verses.38: He who believes in me, as it is written, will have rivers of living water flowing out of his mouth.
verses.39: And this is what he said about the spirit that the believers were to receive from Him. After all, it was not really a spirit at all; Jesus never claimed to be a spirit at all.
verses.40: Thus, when they heard these words from the crowd, they said, “Is he really the prophet?”
verses.41: Others said, “This is indeed the Christ.” But others said, “Surely, the Christ does not come from Galilee.”
verses.42: The text doesn’t say that Christ came from David’s lineage. It only says that Christ came from Bethlehem, the city where David lived.
verses.43: Therefore, a split occurred among the crowd because of him.
verses.44: But no one wanted to touch him at all. No one even touched him with their hands.
verses.45: So, the servants went to the high priests and the Pharisees. They said to them, “Why don’t you bring him here?”
verses.46: The servants replied in that manner. No man could speak like that at all.
verses.47: So, the Pharisees said to them: “Don’t you be deceived by this?”
verses.48: Did not any of the leaders believe in him, or did they believe in him because of the Pharisees?
verses.49: But this crowd, who do not know the law, are indeed wrong.
verses.50: Nikodemus says to them, “The man who came to him before was one of them.”
verses.51: It is not our law that judges a person if he does not first listen to what they are doing.
verses.52: They also said to him, “Don’t you come from Galilee either?” They tried to deceive him, but they realized that the prophet did not come from Galilee at all.
verses.53: And each one was sent to his own house.
